name: tdd
description: Build features or fix bugs with red-green-refactor. Test-first, behavior-driven, no shortcuts.

steps.name: Plan
steps.instruction: Read project context. Check ADRs in the area you are touching. Confirm the behavior list and interface design with the user before writing code.

steps.name: Endpoint scope check
steps.instruction: Verify the slice covers every endpoint it should per the registry. Read the issue tracker issue (Linear/GitHub) if one exists for this slice and check acceptance criteria.
checklist: Endpoint registry checked - every 'in' endpoint for this slice is covered
Issue tracker issue read if it exists

steps.name: Tracer bullet
steps.instruction: Write one end-to-end test that exercises the happy path through the public interface. It must fail (red).
checklist: Test exercises happy path through public interface

steps.name: Incremental loop
steps.instruction: For each behavior: write a failing test (red), implement the minimum code to pass (green), then refactor. Show the user each test before writing implementation. Proceed with your ranking but give the opportunity to redirect.
per_cycle_checklist: Code is minimal for this test

steps.name: Refactor
steps.instruction: Clean up implementation and tests. Consult reference docs for patterns. Check slice-marker.md for done-marker semantics when the slice is complete.
checklist: Interfaces are deep (few methods, rich behavior)
Slice done marker written if slice complete (reference/slice-marker.md)

steps.name: Convention enforcement
steps.instruction: Verify convention-enforcement tests pass if the project has them. If a new convention or repeating pattern emerged during refactor, offer to create a convention test for it.
checklist: New conventions offered as tests if detected during refactor

tone: Disciplined. One test, one implementation, no shortcuts.
